en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province has a nearly perfect cone shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Babuyan Channel.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its brain to help it see at night.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is situated on Volcano Island, which is located right in the middle of Taal Lake.
The Philippines is the world's top producer of abaca, a banana plant whose strong fibers are used to make ropes and currency.
The Philippine Sea, located east of the archipelago, contains the Philippine Trench, which is one of the deepest oceanic trenches on Earth.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The northeast monsoon, called amihan, brings cool and dry air to the Philippines between November and February every year.
Samar is the third-largest island in the Philippines and is located in the Eastern Visayas region, directly east of Leyte.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, has a distinctive crest of dark feathers and primarily hunts monkeys in Mindanao forests.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao province were carved into the mountains over 2,000 years ago by indigenous people using simple tools.
